tldr: SpaceXAI shipped Grok 4.5 on Jul 9, its first Opus-class model since acquiring Cursor. Coverage framed it as the fastest-moving frontier lab shipping yet another release.
whats_new: A day-two benchmark write-up found Grok 4.5 cuts coding-agent cost 80% at near-frontier speed, but with a higher hallucination rate than rival models.
why_it_matters: Grok 4.5's price/speed profile makes it worth a coding-agent cost trial, but its higher hallucination rate means it needs stricter output verification than Opus-class alternatives before production use.

status.detail: Launched Jul 9; a Jul 10 benchmark write-up is the only independent read on cost, speed, and reliability so far.

beats.headline: SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5, its first Opus-class model post Cursor acquisition
beats.summary: AINews/latent_space frames the release as SpaceXAI continuing to out-ship every other frontier lab.

beats.headline: Hands-on benchmark: 80% cheaper coding-agent runs, near-frontier speed, more hallucinations
beats.summary: Tech Times' day-two benchmark is the first independent read on Grok 4.5's coding-agent economics and reliability tradeoff.

open_questions: Does the 80% coding-agent cost cut hold up across benchmarks beyond Tech Times' initial write-up?
How much does the higher hallucination rate cost in practice for agentic coding workflows — does it require extra verification steps that erode the price advantage?
Does SpaceXAI publish its own benchmark numbers, or does independent testing stay the only source?
take_for_builders: If you're evaluating coding-agent cost, benchmark Grok 4.5 against your current model on your own tasks before switching — the 80% cost cut is real per Tech Times, but weigh it against the reported higher hallucination rate for your specific verification budget.
